meta.review_notes: Several categories are unknown because the 41K policy text is silent on camera/microphone, contacts/phonebook, health/biometric, and children's data. All claims were tightened to strict legal-safe language with direct quotes.

app.name: LinkedIn
app.description: A professional networking platform for connecting with colleagues, finding jobs, sharing industry news, and building your career.

verdict.one_liner: LinkedIn shares your data with Microsoft and advertisers, and your public posts can spread widely.
verdict.summary: LinkedIn collects extensive professional and personal data and shares it with Microsoft affiliates, service providers, and advertisers using hashed identifiers. Your public content can be re-shared anywhere. Device and usage tracking is extensive, including cross-device recognition and ad targeting outside certain countries. Account deletion is available within about 30 days, and job searches are not shared with employers. However, several categories are not addressed in the policy text, creating uncertainty.
verdict.recommendation_reason: LinkedIn states it shares your data with Microsoft and advertisers, tracks your behavior across devices, and allows public content to spread beyond the platform. Several data practices are not clearly explained in the policy.

red.title: Shares data with Microsoft for ads
red.plain_english: LinkedIn states it may share your personal data with Microsoft and other affiliates to improve, provide, or develop advertising services.

red.title: Public posts can spread beyond LinkedIn
red.plain_english: When you post publicly on LinkedIn, your content can be viewed by anyone and re-shared anywhere, according to the policy.

red.title: Tracks your device across services
red.plain_english: LinkedIn uses cookies, pixels, and device IDs to recognize you and your devices on, off, and across different services and devices where you have engaged with LinkedIn. Outside certain countries, it may also collect device data even when you have not used LinkedIn.

red.title: May share data in a sale or merger
red.plain_english: LinkedIn states it can share your personal data as part of a sale, merger, or change in control, and any buyer may continue to use it under this policy.

green.title: Account deletion available
green.plain_english: You can close your LinkedIn account, and your profile generally stops being visible within 24 hours. Closed account information is usually deleted within 30 days.

green.title: Job searches hidden from employer
green.plain_english: LinkedIn states it does not share your job hunting or personal messages with your employer unless you choose to share them.

categories.label: Camera & Microphone
categories.plain_english: LinkedIn's privacy policy does not clearly state whether the app accesses your camera or microphone.
categories.detail: The policy mentions videos and content but does not explicitly address device camera or microphone access.
concerns: Policy is silent on camera and microphone access

categories.label: Location & GPS
categories.plain_english: LinkedIn may collect your precise location if you opt in, for features like suggesting nearby members. The policy does not clearly explain how your general location is determined.
categories.detail: GPS is opt-in for specific features. IP address is collected but the policy does not explicitly link it to location inference.
categories.policy_excerpt: If you use our Services from a mobile device, that device will send us data about your location based on your phone settings. We will ask you to opt-in before we use GPS or other tools to identify your precise location.

categories.label: Contacts & Phonebook
categories.plain_english: LinkedIn's policy does not clearly state whether the app accesses your phone's contacts. It says others may import contact information about you, and you may choose to send contacts from Microsoft apps.
categories.detail: The policy describes others uploading contacts and email sync, but does not explicitly say the mobile app reads your phonebook.
categories.policy_excerpt: We receive personal data (including contact information) about you when others import or sync their calendar with our Services, associate their contacts with Member profiles, scan and upload business cards, or send messages using our Services.
concerns: Policy is silent on mobile contacts access
Others may upload your contact info without your consent

categories.label: Storage & File Access
categories.plain_english: LinkedIn collects files and information when you upload them, such as a resume or calendar data.
categories.detail: User-initiated uploads for resumes, forms, and calendar syncs. No mention of broad storage scanning.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect personal data from you when you provide, post or upload it to our Services, such as when you fill out a form, (e.g., with demographic data or salary), respond to a survey, or submit a resume or fill out a job application on our Services.

categories.label: Data Sharing with 3rd Parties
categories.plain_english: LinkedIn states it shares your data with Microsoft and other affiliates for advertising and service development. It also shares hashed identifiers with advertisers, and may disclose data for legal reasons or during a sale.
categories.detail: Shared with Microsoft, affiliates, service providers, advertisers (hashed IDs/device identifiers), and under legal demands. May share during mergers.
categories.policy_excerpt: We may also share with our Affiliates, including Microsoft, your personal data to improve, provide or develop their advertising services.

categories.label: Account & Identity Data
categories.plain_english: LinkedIn collects extensive identity and professional data, and may receive additional data about you from employers, partners, and Microsoft.
categories.detail: Name, email, phone, password, profile fields, resume, employer data, and Microsoft affiliate data collected.
categories.policy_excerpt: To create an account you need to provide data including your name, email address and/or mobile number, general location (e.g., city), and a password.
concerns: Data received from employers and partners

categories.label: Behavioural & Ad Tracking
categories.plain_english: LinkedIn tracks your searches, content views, clicks, and device information to show you targeted ads, and may collect data about your device even when you have not used LinkedIn.
categories.detail: Extensive tracking via cookies, pixels, device IDs, IP, usage logs. Cross-device and cross-service tracking. Targeted ads on and off platform.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect data through cookies and similar technologies (e.g., pixels and ad tags) to collect data (e.g., device IDs) to recognize you and your device(s) on, off and across different services and devices where you have engaged with our Services.
concerns: Targeted ads on and off platform
Device data collected even without engagement

categories.label: Children's Data Handling
categories.plain_english: LinkedIn's privacy policy does not clearly explain how it handles children's data or what age limits apply.
categories.detail: No explicit mention of children's data safeguards or age requirements in the policy text.

categories.label: Network & Internet Activity
categories.plain_english: LinkedIn collects your IP address, browser details, cookie IDs, and the web pages you visit before and after using the service. This may be used for ads outside certain countries.
categories.detail: IP, referrer URLs, cookies, device info logged. Used for security and ad relevance outside Designated Countries.
categories.policy_excerpt: We receive information about your network and device (e.g., IP address, proxy server, operating system, web browser and add-ons, device identifier and features, cookie IDs and/or ISP, or your mobile carrier).

categories.label: Device Info & Fingerprinting
categories.plain_english: LinkedIn collects device identifiers, browser details, and cookie IDs to recognize you across devices and services.
categories.detail: Device IDs, browser info, cookies, pixel tags used for cross-device recognition and advertising.
categories.policy_excerpt: We collect data through cookies and similar technologies (e.g., pixels and ad tags) to collect data (e.g., device IDs) to recognize you and your device(s) on, off and across different services and devices.

categories.label: Health & Biometric Data
categories.plain_english: LinkedIn's privacy policy does not mention health or biometric data.
categories.detail: No explicit mention of health, fitness, or biometric data collection.
concerns: Policy silent on health and biometric data

categories.label: Financial & Payment Data
categories.plain_english: LinkedIn collects payment and billing information if you sign up for premium services, and may use a third-party payment processor.
categories.detail: Credit card and billing info for premium. Third-party processor used.
categories.policy_excerpt: If you register for a premium Service, you will need to provide payment (e.g., credit card) and billing information.

categories.label: Data Deletion & User Rights
categories.plain_english: You can delete your LinkedIn account, and your profile usually stops being visible within 24 hours. Full deletion typically takes about 30 days, but some data may be kept for legal or security reasons.
categories.detail: Deletion rights available. 24h visibility stop, 30 days typical deletion. Legal/security retention applies. Shared content may persist.
categories.policy_excerpt: If you choose to close your LinkedIn account, your personal data will generally stop being visible to others on our Services within 24 hours. We generally delete closed account information within 30 days of account closure, except as noted below.
concerns: Some data retained after account closure

categories.label: Policy Change Notification
categories.plain_english: LinkedIn may change its privacy policy and will notify you of material changes. If you continue using the service, you accept the updated policy. You can close your account if you object.
categories.detail: Notice for material changes via Service. Continued use = acceptance. Account closure is the opt-out.
categories.policy_excerpt: LinkedIn can modify this Privacy Policy, and if we make material changes to it, we will provide notice through our Services, or by other means, to provide you the opportunity to review the changes before they become effective. If you object to any changes, you may close your account.
